text: In 2011 the Court sided with AT&T, five to four. Justice Antonin Scalia wrote it. A state cannot refuse to enforce a class action waiver because it finds it unfair.
provenance: In 2011, the Supreme Court sided with AT&T. By a vote of five to four, it held that the Federal Arbitration Act preempts California's rule — that a state cannot refuse to enforce a class-action waiver just because it finds the waiver unfair.
The opinion was written by Justice Antonin Scalia.

text: Justice Stephen Breyer dissented. For claims worth a few dollars, the class action is often the only realistic way to hold a large company accountable. Take that away, and the case may end before it starts.
provenance: For claims worth only a few dollars each, he argued, the class action is often the only realistic way to hold a large company accountable at all. Take it away, and you have not just changed the forum — you may have ended the case before it starts.
